title: Trump Defends Calling Putin a 'Friend' While Sidestepping U.S. Alliance
snippet: President Donald Trump doubled down on his personal relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin following a trip to Asia, claiming both Moscow and Kyiv are eager for peace despite a fresh barrage of Russian strikes across Ukraine.
content:
Fresh off a high-stakes diplomatic trip to Asia, President Donald Trump aggressively defended his warm rapport with Vladimir Putin on Friday, standing by his characterization of the Russian leader as a personal "friend" while dodging whether Putin is a friend to the United States.

Speaking during a wide-ranging White House press briefing, Trump insisted that his personal ties with foreign strongmen—including Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping—are crucial assets for American diplomacy, particularly in brokering an end to Russia's war in Ukraine.

'Stuck in It': Trump Blames Both Leaders for Continued Fighting

Despite Moscow launching one of its heaviest bombardments against Ukrainian targets just hours after Putin and Trump met in China, the U.S. president cast Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as equally responsible for the ongoing stalemate.

“He’d love to end the war,” Trump said of the Russian chief, arguing that both leaders want to stop the fighting but lack a clear exit strategy. “You have two guys that don’t know how to end it. We’re trying to help them. You have two people that hate each other, Zelenskyy and Putin. They don’t know how to end it. They want to end it. They’re both stuck in it.”

When directly asked whether he considers Putin a friend to the American nation, Trump demurred. “I can’t speak to America,” he said, before immediately highlighting his long history with Putin and reiterating past grievances over federal investigations into 2016 election interference.

Diplomatic Friction and Escalating Strikes

Trump’s remarks came as Russia launched a massive night attack against Ukraine, firing over 400 drones and 110 missiles—including ballistic weapons and cluster munitions—that killed at least eight civilians and wounded dozens more, according to Ukrainian officials. Tensions also spilled into NATO territory after two Russian missiles and a drone crossed into Poland during military exercises.

Meanwhile, cracks emerged over potential peace negotiations. After U.S. envoy Jared Kushner suggested Russia might tolerate NATO-style Article 5 defense guarantees for a post-war Ukraine, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov promptly rejected the idea, stating that even "quasi-membership" in NATO is unacceptable to Moscow.

Trump brushed aside Russia's public pushback, characterizing it as routine posturing in a wider public relations contest.

Rubio Defends Engagement With Autocrats

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who joined Trump at the press conference, pushed back against critics who accuse the administration of being overly cozy with authoritarian rulers.

“I want everybody to understand the relationships between heads of state are invaluable,” Rubio said, emphasizing that personal rapport sets the stage for trade negotiators and diplomats across the administration.
